questions.q:
The pressure $P$ of a gas corresponding to various volumes $V$ is recorded:

| $V$ (cm³) | 50 | 60 | 70 | 90 | 100 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $P$ (kg/cm²) | 64.7 | 51.3 | 40.5 | 25.9 | 7.8 |

The ideal gas law is given by the function form $PV^\gamma = C$, where $\gamma$ and $C$ are constants.

**(a)** Estimate the constants $\gamma$ and $C$.

**(b)** Use the least-squares line to predict the value of the pressure $P$ of a gas corresponding to the volume $110$ cm³.
questions.explanation: By linearizing $PV^\gamma = C$ via logarithms, we apply simple linear regression on $(\ln V, \ln P)$ to estimate $\gamma$ (slope magnitude) and $C$ (from intercept), then back-transform to predict $P$.
questions.answer:
**(a)** Taking logarithms: $\ln P = \ln C - \gamma \ln V$, so let $y = \ln P$, $x = \ln V$, $\beta_0 = \ln C$, $\beta_1 = -\gamma$.

Compute the transformed values:

| $x = \ln V$ | $y = \ln P$ |
|---|---|
| 3.912 | 4.170 |
| 4.094 | 3.937 |
| 4.248 | 3.701 |
| 4.500 | 3.254 |
| 4.605 | 2.055 |

$\bar{x} = 4.272$, $\bar{y} = 3.423$

$$\hat{\beta}_1 = \frac{\sum x_i y_i - n\bar{x}\bar{y}}{\sum x_i^2 - n\bar{x}^2} \approx -1.49$$

So $\gamma \approx 1.49$

$$\hat{\beta}_0 = \bar{y} - \hat{\beta}_1 \bar{x} \approx 3.423 + 1.49 \times 4.272 \approx 9.788$$

So $\ln C \approx 9.788 \Rightarrow C \approx e^{9.788} \approx 17888$

**(b)** For $V = 110$ cm³: $x = \ln(110) \approx 4.700$

$$\hat{y} = 9.788 - 1.49 \times 4.700 \approx 2.787$$

$$\hat{P} = e^{2.787} \approx 16.23 \text{ kg/cm}^2$$

questions.q:
The following data shows marks achieved in Mathematics and English exams:

| English | 56 | 75 | 45 | 71 | 61 | 64 | 58 | 80 | 76 | 61 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mathematics | 66 | 70 | 40 | 60 | 65 | 56 | 59 | 77 | 67 | 36 |

Find Spearman's rank correlation coefficient.
questions.explanation: Spearman's formula $r_s = 1 - \frac{6\sum d_i^2}{n(n^2-1)}$ measures rank correlation. A value of $\approx 0.646$ indicates a moderately strong positive relationship between English and Mathematics marks.

questions.q:
If the following function is a probability mass function, find the value of $k$:

| $x$ | $-2$ | $-1$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $p(x)$ | $0.2$ | $0.4$ | $k$ | $0.2$ | $0.1$ |

Then determine:

**(a)** $P(X < 2)$

**(b)** $P(X \geq -2)$

**(c)** $P(-1 \leq X \leq 1)$

**(d)** $P(X \leq -2 \text{ or } X = 1)$
questions.explanation: A valid PMF must satisfy $\sum_x p(x) = 1$. Once $k$ is found, probabilities are computed by summing the relevant $p(x)$ values.

questions.q:
A company categorizes emails into work (70%), personal (20%), and spam (10%). Work emails have 2% typos, personal emails have 5%, and spam emails have 15%.

**(a)** If an email is selected at random, what is the probability that it has typos?

**(b)** If an email has typos, what is the probability it is spam?
questions.explanation: Part (a) uses the Law of Total Probability. Part (b) uses Bayes' Theorem to reverse the conditioning — given a typo occurred, we find the probability the email is spam.

questions.q: 20% of customers at a store make a purchase. If 15 customers visit, what is the probability that exactly 4 make a purchase?
questions.explanation: The Binomial formula $P(X=k)=\binom{n}{k}p^k(1-p)^{n-k}$ applies when each customer independently makes a purchase with probability $p=0.2$.
questions.answer:
This is a Binomial distribution with $n=15$, $p=0.2$, $X=4$.

$$P(X=4) = \binom{15}{4}(0.2)^4(0.8)^{11}$$

$$= 1365 \times 0.0016 \times 0.08590 \approx 0.1876$$

questions.q: A call center receives an average of 5 calls per hour. What is the probability of receiving exactly 3 calls in an hour?
questions.explanation: The Poisson PMF $P(X=k) = \frac{e^{-\lambda}\lambda^k}{k!}$ models the number of events in a fixed interval when the average rate $\lambda$ is known.
questions.answer:
This is a Poisson distribution with $\lambda = 5$, $k = 3$.

$$P(X=3) = \frac{e^{-5} \cdot 5^3}{3!} = \frac{e^{-5} \times 125}{6} \approx \frac{0.006738 \times 125}{6} \approx 0.1404$$

questions.q: In meteorology, the intensity of UV-B radiation is classified as: weak, moderate, strong, extreme. What is the best measure for this data?
questions.explanation: UV-B intensity categories are ordinal data. The Mean is inappropriate for ordinal scales; both the Median and Mode are valid measures for ordinal data, making option (d) correct.

questions.q: Which measure of central tendency would best depict the following data: $2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 100$?
questions.explanation: The value 100 is an extreme outlier that heavily distorts the Mean. The Median is resistant to outliers and best represents the center of this skewed dataset.

questions.q: In a class of 100 students there are 80 boys whose average marks in a subject are 70. If the average marks of the complete class is 72, then what is the average of the girls?
questions.explanation: Total marks $= 100 \times 72 = 7200$. Boys' total $= 80 \times 70 = 5600$. Girls' total $= 7200 - 5600 = 1600$. Number of girls $= 20$. Girls' average $= 1600 / 20 = 80$.

questions.q:
The value of $k$ when the probability mass function is given by:
$$P(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{2x}{k}, & x = 1, 2, 3 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}$$
questions.explanation:
$\sum_{x=1}^{3} \frac{2x}{k} = 1 \Rightarrow \frac{2(1)+2(2)+2(3)}{k} = 1 \Rightarrow \frac{2+4+6}{k} = 1 \Rightarrow \frac{12}{k} = 1 \Rightarrow k = 12$.

Wait — re-checking: $\frac{2}{k}+\frac{4}{k}+\frac{6}{k} = \frac{12}{k} = 1 \Rightarrow k = 12$. The correct answer is **(a) 12**.

questions.q: A code consists of a digit chosen from $0$ to $6$ followed by a letter of the alphabet. What is the probability the code is $6Z$?
questions.explanation: Digits from 0 to 6 = 7 choices. Letters of the alphabet = 26 choices. Total codes $= 7 \times 26 = 182$. $P(6Z) = \dfrac{1}{182}$.

questions.explanation: $n = \dfrac{\sum x_i}{\bar{x}} = \dfrac{20}{4} = 5$. For an odd $n=5$, the median is the $\dfrac{n+1}{2} = 3$rd ranked value.

questions.q: If the variance of $x$ is $v(x) = 3$, then $v\!\left(\dfrac{1}{3}x - 5\right) =$
questions.explanation: Using the variance rule $v(aX + b) = a^2 v(X)$: $v\!\left(\frac{1}{3}x - 5\right) = \left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^2 \times 3 = \frac{1}{9} \times 3 = \frac{1}{3}$.
